Issued at 322 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

Tonight through Friday...

This upper level disturbance will continue to push mainly
through he Dakotas tonight, ending up over the MN/Can border 
by sunrise Thursday. The accompanying surface front is expected 
to diminish/wash out as it loses its upper level push...with the
weaker sfc pattern bringing light and at times variable winds 
this evening through the overnight hours. While much lower 
dewpoints will have worked their way into the NWrn half of the 
forecast area...that push doesn't look to get all the way 
through, keeping some lower level moisture around...and with the
light winds and little sky cover, models continue to show the 
potential for the development of fog as we get closer to sunrise
Thursday into the mid-morning hours. Best potential for fog 
(visibilities under 1 mile are possible) looks to be roughly 
along/south of a line Geneva, NE to Phillipsburg, KS.

Outside of that fog/lower level stratus potential into the
morning hours, overall Thursday doesn't look to be too bad of 
a day...and honestly looks to be the nicest day of this 7-day 
forecast period. Expecting generally partly cloudy skies...with 
winds turning back to the south as sfc low pressure starts to 
reorganized ahead of the next upper level system, speeds for 
much of the area look to top out around 10-15 MPH, though the 
WSWrn half could have afternoon gusts closer to 20 MPH. Highs 
look to reach right around 60 in the NW to mid-60s in the SW.

Dry conditions are forecast to continue on into Friday, but the 
winds will be cranking back up. Overall, hasn't been any notable
changes in models...after a bit of a lull, stronger southwesterly
flow aloft returns, as that system currently moving onto the 
West Coast pushes further inland. By the end of the day on 
Friday, models aren't in too bad of agreement, showing the main 
upper level low over the western half of Canada, with troughing 
extend southward through the Rockies into western portions of 
the Desert SW. While the forecast remains dry with this system 
still off to the west...surface low pressure will continue to 
deepen as the system approaches, bringing increasing southerly 
winds to the entire forecast area. Sustained speeds in the 25-30
MPH range are not out of the question, along with the potential
for gusts exceeding 40 MPH. So although forecast high temps are
a touch warmer than Thursday with more mid-upper 60s, the winds
will make for a less pleasant day. 

This weekend into next week... 

During the weekend through Monday time frame...any precipitation 
chances in the forecast remaining focused on the Saturday-
Saturday night time frame. Models aren't in too bad of agreement
looking at the big picture in the upper levels...showing that 
above mentioned troughing continuing to work its way east 
through the Rockies and onto the High Plains through the first 
half of the day Saturday...though there are still some 
differences with finer details like the timing and exact 
location of precipitation. A swath of precip running from the 
Srn Plains up into the western Great Lakes looks to develop by 
early afternoon, as large scale lift increases between the 
shortwave troughing emerging from the Central/Srn Rockies and 
the more organized low over the US/Can border...but models vary 
with the timing some with the onset and spread of precipitation 
chances (earlier aftn vs mid-late aftn). Not only are their some
uncertainties with the timing...there are also question with 
how much of our forecast area is impacted by any precip. At this
point, more model support shows at least the eastern half of 
the forecast area sees measurable rain...a few suggest the main 
axis could largely miss our area to the east. Will see how 
models trend. Outside of those chances, the forecast dries back 
out for Sunday and Monday...with models showing a more 
zonal/progressive upper level pattern building in across the 
region. 

As far as temperatures go Saturday-Monday...the accompanying
surface cold front and cooler air looks to be working its way 
through the forecast area on Saturday, making for a tricky/lower
confidence forecast. Current forecast highs range from the 
mid-40s in the NW to low-60s SE...those warmer temps likely 
occurring on the earlier side of things. In the wake of that 
front...highs on Sun-Mon top out in the 40s.

Looking at the mid-late week period/Thanksgiving Day...our first 
snowflakes of the season may be arriving on Tuesday. Not worth 
getting too hung up on details this far out...plenty of model 
uncertainties to work out. Models are showing a shortwave 
disturbance embedded in this more zonal flow working its way 
through the Rockies to start off the new work week...moving 
through the Plains roughly in the Tuesday day-evening time 
frame. At this point, timing isn't too off between models...but 
there are differences whether it's more of closed low or an open
wave. Looks to be quicker- hitting system...lac
